thread:
Jordan: Heads up — we've got a spike in p95 and p99 latency for the /v1/generate endpoint hitting US‑EAST started ~1814999800. Support is seeing customer complaints. graphs show queue depth climbing and requests timing out.:warning:
Mei: I see it on the dashboard, p95 doubled to ~420ms, p99 ~1.2s. Concurrent inflight requests to the model pool are maxed. queue_length histogram shows long tail.
Ravi: Any recent deploys or config changes?
Jordan: We rolled the routing/placement change last night (deploy 2026-03-14 23:45) that pins region affinity and bumped per-worker max inflight from 32 -> 48 for a perf experiment.
Mei: That matches. I pulled the admission-controller logs. Lots of "delayed_enqueue" and "burst_bucket_refill" warnings. Snippet: ```text
[2026-03-15T03:02:12Z] admission-controller: delayed_enqueue model=text-gen-v2 worker=we-042 queue=127
[2026-03-15T03:02:15Z] admission-controller: refill_rate too low for burst, allow_on_overflow=false
```
Alex: There's also a routing hotfix that moved 15% of traffic from eu-west to us-east for capacity tests. That probably concentrated load.
Ravi: Ok likely scenario = concentrated traffic + higher per-worker concurrency -> longer scheduling latencies -> KV cache pressure -> higher token latency and tail.
Jordan: Support reports some 429s then timeouts. Can we triage quick mitigations?
Mei: Short list: 1) roll back per-worker concurrency bump (set max_inflight back to 32) 2) enable early-reject on admission controller for requests > 10s queue wait 3) divert canary traffic off us-east 15% back to eu-west 4) enable fallback smaller model (text-gen-v2-quant) for lower priority traffic.
Ravi: I can push 1 and 2 as hotfixes. Command to update admission controller config: ```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://infra-api/configs/admission" -d '{"max_inflight":32,"early_reject_threshold_ms":10000}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'
```
Ravi: Also I want to flip allow_on_overflow=true temporarily to prevent long queueing until we fix routing.
Alex: I'll open a traffic shift: loadbalancer rule rollback to move 15% back. Doing gradual 5% steps.
Mei: I'll watch metrics. Adding a temporary alert: queue_length > 80 for 5m -> page oncall.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-01 — elevated request queueing/us-east. Pager duty: oncall-sre.
Jordan: After Ravi's change, queue_length dropped from ~120 to ~30 in ~6 minutes. p95 went from 420ms -> 180ms. p99 down to ~420ms. Looks promising.
Ravi: Confirmed. I left fallback model routing enabled for low-priority keys. No 500s after shift.
Mei: Repro steps for postmortem notes: 1) run loadtest with region-shift config: `wrk -t16 -c200 -d5m https://api.redwood/v1/generate` 2) set per-worker max_inflight 48 and observe queue growth 3) enable routing shift 15% -> observe amplification.
Alex: Followups: - create canary gating for routing config changes (must ramp at 1%/5m and failback on increased p95) - add a daily job that samples queue length per region and alerts on >50th percentile jumps - add unit test for admission-controller refill logic.
Jordan: Action items: Ravi to PR hotfix and make emergency rollback permanent until we can run a canary; Mei to own graphs + alert tuning; Alex to own routing canary gating; I'll file postmortem and customer notes.
Ravi: PR drafted: https://git.internal/r/admission/+/I-834-hotfix — will merge after one ack.
Mei: I'll update #support with provisional message: "We've identified elevated tail latencies tied to routing + concurrency change. Temporary mitigations applied; full postmortem forthcoming."
Jordan: Thanks team. We'll keep this thread as the timeline for the incident. Please add any logs or steps you used to debug.
Alex: Adding final note — once we stabilize, we should run traffic replay against dedicated staging with the new concurrency to measure KV cache eviction effects.
Mei: Closing loop: 30m after fixes p95 ~160ms, p99 ~380ms, errors back to baseline. Marking incident as resolved but postmortem required.
Jordan: Filing postmortem now. INC-2026-0315-01 -> postmortem link will be posted here when ready. :white_check_mark:
